evals.prompt: Read this SPEC.md and tell me what's implemented vs. still pending.
evals.expected_output: A clear summary of the task tracker's intent, sections present, and a call-out that task priority levels (under Future Considerations) are not yet implemented.
expectations: Explicitly identifies task priority levels as not yet implemented
Does not claim priority levels are already implemented
References the API endpoints listed in the spec
Does not create or modify any files

evals.prompt: Sync this SPEC.md with the current codebase.
evals.expected_output: SPEC.md updated to add the undocumented PATCH /tasks/{id}/complete endpoint (additive), a flagged contradiction between the spec's Task.status enum and the code's boolean completed field (not silently resolved), and the priority levels Future Consideration left untouched since it isn't implemented yet.
expectations: SPEC.md's API section is updated to include PATCH /tasks/{id}/complete
The priority levels Future Consideration item is still present, not removed
The contradiction between the spec's Task.status enum and the code's boolean completed field is flagged or called out, not silently overwritten in either direction
No existing requirement or feature is deleted solely because it isn't implemented yet
The original metadata (author, updated) is left untouched, not edited or removed

evals.prompt: Generate a SPEC.md for this codebase.
evals.expected_output: A new SPEC.md grounded in the actual code (Express task API with CRUD routes plus the complete endpoint), not invented structure, and not assuming features the code doesn't have (e.g. no status enum or priority levels). Grounded detail (e.g. Testing/Issues noting real gaps like missing validation or persistence) is welcome since it's verifiable from the code.
expectations: The API section lists all 6 routes present in the code, including PATCH /tasks/{id}/complete
The API section does not list routes that don't exist in the code
Each API endpoint entry includes a brief description of what it does, not just the bare method and path
No Task.status enum or priority-level fields are invented, since the code has neither
Domain/entity fields described (if present) match the actual Task model: id, title, completed, createdAt
If a Domain section is included, the Task entity's field list appears under Entities as an #### Task heading, not under Types
Frontmatter tech fields with a single item (e.g. a single language or dependency) use inline form (e.g. languages: JavaScript), not a one-item YAML list
metadata does not include a fabricated author value
metadata does not include an updated value on initial creation
If a Deployment-style section for the PORT variable is included, its heading uses a single alias (e.g. '### Environment Variables'), not the full pipe-separated alias list from the schema

evals.prompt: Define a new spec for a static website of car photos.
evals.expected_output: A reasonably fleshed-out new SPEC.md inferred from the description using best judgment (e.g. Features, Requirements, Domain, UI) with assumptions stated explicitly -- not just frontmatter, title, and description, since the user did not ask for a simple/minimal spec.
expectations: Output includes at least Features and/or Requirements beyond just frontmatter, title, and description
Assumptions made beyond the one-sentence prompt are stated explicitly (e.g. in a Considerations/Assumptions subsection), not silently invented
No ## API section is invented, since a static photo website has no backend of its own to expose
If a Domain section is included, entity field lists (e.g. Photo, Album) appear under Entities as #### headings, not under Types
If UI Components are listed, each includes a brief description of its purpose, not just a bare name
If a Folder Structure section is included, it uses a fenced tree view rather than a flat bullet list of paths
Frontmatter tech fields with a single item use inline form, not a one-item YAML list
metadata includes only a created date -- no author, no updated, no changelog entry

evals.prompt: Set up a bare-bones, minimal spec for a personal blog -- just the basics for now.
evals.expected_output: A minimal SPEC.md: frontmatter, title, and a short description only, per the explicit request for something bare-bones/minimal -- no invented sections.
expectations: Output contains only frontmatter, a title, and a short description -- no additional H2 sections
metadata includes only a created date -- no author, no updated, no changelog entry

evals.prompt: Turn this into a more detailed spec with frontmatter. Let's use the latest version of React. Include features, user stories, architecture, and data design.
evals.expected_output: A detailed SPEC.md for a frontend-only React/TypeScript contact management app that persists data through a mocked API layer and browser localStorage, with no real backend yet. Correctly separates the mocked backend contract (External Interfaces) from the domain model (Domain) and from this component's own API surface (none -- omitted).
expectations: No ## API section is created, since this component has no backend of its own to expose
The mocked CRUD service contract (method names with descriptions) lives entirely under External Interfaces, not split into ## API
External Interfaces also describes the localStorage persistence shape and/or key, not just a one-line mention that local storage is used
If a Domain section is included, the primary entity (e.g. Contact) is defined under Entities as an #### heading with its full field list, not under Types
Types (if present) contains only shared constrained value types (enums, formats, small value structs), never the primary entity's field list
If Personas are defined under User Stories, every story's actor is one of the defined personas
If UI Components are listed, each includes a brief description of its purpose, not just a bare name
Sections follow the spec schema's recommended order unless the request implies otherwise
The explicit list of sections named in the prompt (features, user stories, architecture, data design) is treated as emphasis, not exhaustive -- a UI section is still included for a React frontend
Frontmatter tech fields with a single item (e.g. a single language or framework) use inline form, not a one-item YAML list
Frontmatter indentation uses spaces, not tabs
If a Testing section is included, content for each testing domain uses the corresponding ### heading (e.g. ### Unit) rather than an inline bullet label
If a Folder Structure section is included, it uses a fenced tree view rather than a flat bullet list of paths
